subject: Call recap + next steps — token costing and feature payback targets
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@sunrisehealth.com>, Laura Mills <laura.mills@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Subject: Call recap + next steps — token costing and feature payback targets

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Below is a short recap and the numbers we discussed so we can align on next steps.

Quick recap
- Sunrise goal: embed an assistant-driven triage feature in the patient portal; primary KPI is 30% reduction in triage phone volume within 6 months.
- User profile / scale: current MAU ~120k; target pilot cohort 50–80k active users.
- Expected usage (pilot): 0.5–1.0 feature calls per active user per day (conservative range).
- Tokens per call: customer estimate ~1.5k–2.5k tokens (prompt + response).

Pricing & budget signals from call
- Stated budget range for the pilot: $30k–$60k / month (you mentioned flexibility with traction).
- Targeted unit price you referenced: roughly $800–$1,000 per 1M tokens (you labeled $/1M as a target input for evaluation).

Preliminary volume math (pilot ranges)
- Low usage: 50k users * 0.5 calls/day * 30 days = 750k calls/month.
- High usage: 80k users * 1.0 calls/day * 30 days = 2.4M calls/month.
- Tokens/month (1.5k–2.5k per call): ~1.1B — 6.0B tokens/month (wide range for planning).

Requested next steps
1) Can you confirm a preferred pilot cohort size (50k / 65k / 80k)?
2) Confirm the tokens-per-call midpoint you expect (I used 2k tokens for our internal working model).
3) We’ll bake this into a short unit-econ memo and a pilot quote (attachment: cost_model_v2.xlsx) that shows feature-level $/call, projected monthly invoice, and an example CAC-payback calculation.

Attached: draft cost model (spreadsheet) and a 1-page pilot scope. I’ll follow up with a compact unit-econ note in the morning (includes $/1M tokens scenarios and $/feature examples).

Thanks — Mina

- Pilot cohort: leaning toward ~65k active users.
- Tokens per call: we expect 2k on average (we will monitor).

A couple asks for your unit-econ memo:
- Example $/feature at 2k tokens and at 3k tokens (conservative).
- CAC payback examples: 3-month and 6-month targets — show the math.
- If possible, show a committed discount tier (3mo pilot vs 12mo annual commit) and how that impacts payback.

—Mike

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@sunrisehealth.com>, Laura Mills <laura.mills@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Call recap + next steps — token costing and feature payback targets

Mike — great, appreciate the clarity. Below is a compact unit-econ deep-dive using the inputs you confirmed (65k cohort, 2k tokens/call). I’ve included conservative and optimistic columns and two pricing scenarios (your target $900/1M tokens and a baseline list of $1,000/1M tokens).

Assumptions (working)
- Pilot active users: 65,000
- Calls per user per day: 0.75 (midpoint between your 0.5–1.0 range)
- Calls/month = 65,000 * 0.75 * 30 = 1,462,500 calls/month (~1.46M)
- Tokens per call: 2,000 tokens (you confirmed)
- Tokens/month = 1.46M * 2,000 = 2.925B tokens/month

Redwood inferred inference cost (our internal operating estimate for a production quantized model + batching):
- Estimated inference cost: $220 per 1M tokens (this is our conservative internal marginal cost at pilot scale; dedicated / quantization changes can reduce this).
- Cost per token = $220 / 1,000,000 = $0.00022
- Cost per 2k-token call = 2,000 * $0.00022 = $0.44 per call

Customer pricing scenarios (revenue per 1M tokens)
1) Target price: $900 / 1M tokens => revenue per token = $0.00090 => rev per 2k-token call = $1.80
2) Baseline list: $1,000 / 1M tokens => rev per call = $2.00

Per-call economics (2k tokens/call)
- Scenario A (target $900): rev/call $1.80 — cost/call $0.44 => gross contribution/call $1.36 (~76% gross margin)
- Scenario B (list $1,000): rev/call $2.00 — cost/call $0.44 => gross contribution/call $1.56 (~78% gross margin)

Monthly totals (with 1.46M calls)
- Tokens/month ~2.925B => bill at $900/1M => ~$2,632.5k (i.e., $2.63M) — note: pilot-scale invoice will be in the mid/high hundreds of thousands; this demonstrates scaling risk (we should confirm invoicing cadence and pre-commit vs monthly).
- Cost to Redwood at $220/1M => ~$643.5k/month (our estimate)
- Gross contribution to customer (difference) ~ $1,989k / month in Scenario A (before their incremental costs).

$ / feature and $ per user examples
- Revenue per call (Scenario A) = $1.80. If an active user uses the feature 10 times/month => revenue/user/month = $18; cost/user/month = $4.40 => contribution/user/month = $13.60.

CAC payback (examples)
- If CAC = $80 per new user: at $13.60 contribution/month => payback ~ 5.9 months (meets a 6-month target).
- If CAC = $150 per new user: payback ~ 11 months (misses 6-month target).
- 3-month payback target requires CAC <= $40 given the same contribution profile.

Commit / discount sensitivity (high level)
- 3-month pilot (no commit): list-like pricing ($1,000/1M) or small pilot discount — payback stretched due to shorter observation window; recommend a usage-based pilot with a $/1M pilot tier around $900 and a 12-week milestone credit to offset onboarding friction.
- 12-month commit (volume tier): we can offer a stepped discount (example: 10% at 3B+/month, 18% at 6B+/month) which materially improves payback for you and stabilizes unit economics for both sides. I’ll work up two commitment options in the formal quote.

Next steps (action items)
1) I’ll send a one-page unit-econ memo and two formal quote options (pilot-only and 12-month commit) by EOD today (attached spreadsheet shows the numbers above).
2) Please confirm target pilot cohort (65k confirmed?) and whether you want the pilot priced monthly or invoiced as a single pre-paid credit.
3) We’ll include a short SLA/rollback clause for model availability and a 30-day data retention summary in the pilot SOW.

If helpful I can also show a per-feature sensitivity table (tokens per call 1.5k / 2k / 3k) — I included a quick example in the attached sheet.

Happy to jump on 15–20 min to run through the numbers with you and your finance partner.

Thanks — Mina
